$description: StoryArc colour tokens. Authored in OKLCH, generated to sRGB hex for Swift and Kotlin. Never hardcode a colour in app code — reference a token.
$direction: Editorial darkroom. Chrome recedes so cover art and pages are the loudest thing on screen. Neutrals carry a warm ink tilt (hue ~70) rather than the clinical blue-grey most reader apps default to; light theme is book stock, not paper-white.

ember.use: Primary accent on dark surfaces. Reading-lamp amber. Chrome-only — in-content accents defer to cover-derived colour.

emberStrong.use: Pressed state, and the light-theme accent where 70% lightness would fail contrast on paper.

emberMuted.use: Accent at rest on dark surfaces: progress rails, unselected indicators.

ink.use: Secondary. Indigo ink for links, informational chips, and the second series in charts.

clay.use: The Natural theme's accent on its dark variant. Earthier than ember, so Natural is a theme rather than the same app in beige.

clayStrong.use: The Natural theme's accent on its light variant, where clay at 66% lightness would fail on warm paper.

surfaceOverlay.use: Menus, popovers, the fallback fill behind Liquid Glass when transparency is reduced.

surfaceReader.use: Reader background. Deliberately not #000 — pure black smears on OLED during page turns and kills glass refraction.

surfaceSunken.use: Inset wells: search fields, empty states, cover letterboxing.

scrim.use: Modal scrim at 60% alpha; reader chrome gradient.

surfaceReader.use: Reflowable-text reader background. Book stock cream.

$oledDarkNote: True black chrome for OLED panels, where black draws no power. `surfaceReader` deliberately stays above true black: pure black smears during a page turn, which is the exact motion this app is built around. The setting is honoured where it helps and explained where it does not.

surfaceRaised.use: Cards, list rows, sheets — lifted off black so structure is still readable.

surfaceReader.use: Reader background. Above true black on purpose — see $oledDarkNote.

borderSubtle.use: Hairlines. Carries more weight here, since there is no surface tint to separate rows.

textPrimary.use: Titles and body. Not pure white — reduces halation against true black.

$naturalNote: Natural is a theme, not an appearance: it carries paper texture and an earthier accent, and has its own light and dark variants. Accents reach the whole app so the theme is coherent; the grain is confined to reading surfaces, because texture behind a dense settings list reads as noise rather than as paper.

surfaceReader.use: Reader background. The one surface that carries the paper grain.

textPrimary.use: Titles and body. Warm near-brown rather than neutral ink.

surfaceReader.use: Reader background. The one surface that carries the paper grain.

textPrimary.use: Titles and body. Warm cream rather than neutral white.

warning.use: Stale cache, partial download, degraded connection.

danger.use: Auth failure, unreadable file, destructive action.

offline.use: Source disconnected. Neutral, never red — offline is normal, not an error.

downloaded.use: Available offline. The one badge allowed to compete with cover art.

$readingThemesNote: The six reading-theme presets from openspec/specs/reading-themes. Each is a background and text pair held to WCAG AAA (7:1), because this text is read for hours rather than glanced at. `original` overrides nothing in the publication — its pair exists only to draw its swatch in the preset grid.

original.use: Swatch only. Original leaves publisher styles on and overrides no colour.

quiet.use: Low-contrast dark. Soft off-white on deep neutral, tightened spacing.

paper.use: Neutral light. Book-stock white, serif, comfortable default spacing.

bold.use: High contrast, heavier weight, wider spacing. Low vision without leaving the aesthetic.

calm.use: Warm dim. Cream on brown, generous line height. Long evening sessions.

focus.use: Narrow measure, high contrast, minimal decoration. Fewest words per line.
